prerequisites: Knowledge of machine elements (shafts, axles, screws) as well as statics and strength of materials, manufacturing technology.

learning_outcomes.text: Students will possess fundamental knowledge of load capacity calculation for gears and clutches, and can illustrate their importance for the drivetrain.
They can conceive drivetrains, calculate the load capacity of gears, and design clutches according to recognized technical standards.
Students can assess resource usage in relevant product life phases and decide how to design the drivetrain sustainably.
Students analyze requirements, apply market-standard software tools for component calculation, design components and assemblies, and thus develop sustainable drivetrains for machines.
Students develop solutions for scientific tasks in groups and present the results using meaningful documentation.
Students recognize societal challenges and develop goals and solutions for the given task field.

syllabus_topics: Sustainable design of components and assemblies
Gears as a means to reduce material and energy consumption
Geometry and engagement ratios for spur and helical gearing
Geometry of gears with profile shift
Principle of design for shaft and shifting clutches
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a written exam. The ungraded assessment is a homework assignment, which involves completing 1-2 designs of assemblies including associated calculations. It is recommended to complete the homework before taking the exam. The exam duration is specified in the valid study regulations.
